note: Designer commentary, not enforceable rules text. Included for completeness/context; downstream tools should not treat these as rules to implement.

designRationale.note: Following playtesting that found units took too long to inflict meaningful damage, most Damage 1 weapon profiles across Generic Units (and PC equipment, see equipment/) gained +1 Attack. Damage 2+ and other already-high-volume profiles instead kept their listed Attacks and gained a thematic Anti-[Type] 2 (occasionally 3), so stronger single Hits remain distinct from higher-volume weapons rather than simply becoming strictly better.
The standard Ranged Infantry Shortbow is now 8" / 2 / 5+ / 1. Other weapons purchase greater attack volume, more range, Damage 2, or Firearm traits, usually with a mobility or price trade-off.

Infantry ranged weapons primarily operate within 6–11" normal Range, with Longbows extending farther at the cost of a combined Attack pool reduction. Rangefinder Training adds +2" normal Range, while Longshot Training uses Long Range and the same pool reduction. Artillery remains the main long-range specialist at approximately 15–18".

Up to 10 Models, but additional Models cost 25 Points and Veterans adds +15 more per added Model. A paid ranged weapon also adds +5 per added Model. W1 defenses, concentrated deployment, and one activation per Unit remain important costs.

designRationale.topic: Veterans pricing is per-unit, not uniform
designRationale.note: Veterans grants a flat +1 Attack per Model plus a Hit improvement, so its value scales directly with a Unit's Model count. Larger formations pay more: Line Infantry and Ranged Infantry pay +75 (5-10 and 4-9 Models respectively), each with its own printed per-added-Model Veteran reinforcement surcharge (+10 for Line Infantry, +15 for Ranged Infantry). Smaller or single-Model formations — Elite Infantry (3-5 Models), Cavalry (3-5 Models), Captains and Wizards (1 Model) — pay a flat +50. Generic Supports retain a reduced +25 combat-training option. Veteran bonuses increase the selected weapon's Attacks per Model and improve Hit one step; they do not buff unrelated profiles.

A broadly available upgrade (Line Infantry, Ranged Infantry, Elite Infantry, Cavalry, Captains, Wizards) letting a Unit choose any one Faction, Unit Type, or Trait tag and grant one selected weapon Anti-[chosen tag] 2. Because Anti-[Type] bonuses apply once to the whole Unit's combined Attack pool rather than per Model, this upgrade does not scale with Model count the way Veterans does — it stays a flat, situational bonus regardless of formation size, which is why it is priced as a single flat cost rather than per-unit like Veterans.

Rebuilt around a W2 / Arm 6+ / Eva 6+, Unarmored baseline for the same 75 Points, trading the old flat 5+ Armor for more Wounds and a cheaper, individually purchasable path back to better Armor (Armor and Shields upgrades, each +15, stacking to the old Arm 4+ ceiling). Spears and Polearms have Charge defenses, Heavy Weapons provide Damage 2 with Anti-Armored 2 and the Heavy restriction (its circumstantial extra-dice potential is strong enough on a multi-Model Unit to warrant the movement tradeoff), and Dual Weapons provide volume. Charge Drill, Shock Training, and Brace Training add independent tactical choices. Polearms remain the only melee weapon not implicitly Heavy despite their weight.

New Trait tag, the counterpart to Armored. Granted by baseline Line Infantry; removed once the Armor upgrade is purchased. See rulebooks/chapters/02_wargame/05_unit_tags.md for full rules, including Anti-Unarmored X.

Strong W4 profiles remain their principal distinction. Secondary ranged weapons are allowed without buying Veterans, and their Weapon Mastery/Critical upgrades modify one combined Unit pool rather than multiplying with Model count.

Sneaks, Thralls, and Corpse Horde were buffed by adding Models at unchanged Points (Sneaks +1, Thralls +2, Corpse Horde +3) rather than by adding Attacks, preserving their characteristically fragile, high-casualty-tolerance profile while improving their staying power and board presence.

Two W3 Models remain standard. Additional Models cost +50 but never multiply Commands. Engineer Pistols and the Alchemist/Cleric options are deliberately limited compared with PC class Formulas and spells. Heralds, Scouts/Spotters, Engineers, Alchemists, and Clerics may each learn Target Analysis (+20 Points), a 1 CP Assault Command granting a friendly Unit's next Attack a specialization-appropriate Anti-[Type] 3. It is priced higher than a weapon's own Anti-[Type] 2 precisely because, unlike an owned weapon, a granted Command bonus doesn't scale with the receiving Unit's size or equipment.

The entire Unit Attack pool receives its printed Accurate X, Critical X, etc. once. Distinct applicable keyword bonuses add their X values unless a specific rule states otherwise. An explicit per-Model Attack bonus is different from a Unit Attack-pool bonus.

quickRangedOffensiveComparison.description: Expected raw successful Hits and nominal Damage before enemy Saves, for four Models using a single regular Assault Attack. Nominal Damage is not equivalent to casualties: excess Damage against low-Wound Models can be wasted. Accurate/Surge/Critical or conditional effects are excluded where indicated.

playtestingPriority: Compare four-, six-, eight-, and ten-Model Veteran formations, particularly Damage 2 Heavy Crossbows/Muskets, in full 2,000-point armies with eight matched-play CP cards. Test Charges and Cover alongside ranged output, not just stationary gunlines. Also compare generic support Commands against named faction specialists; all Point costs remain subject to adjustment.
